paragraphs: One-sentence judgement: an athlete or sports competitor does not simply like sport but trains continuously under established rules according to a training and competition plan, competes as planned, reviews and adjusts afterwards, and at the same time manages physical condition, equipment, injury and contracts; the role links training execution, competition performance, body management and external representation into a long-term reviewable chain; people who only want to play and are unwilling to repeat training and review over the long term are not suited.

Signals for continued exploration: you can complete daily training according to the coach and the training plan and record it truthfully, are willing to adjust according to the rules when injury or form fluctuates and to accept the judgement of the team doctor and coach, can restrain yourself under the rules and anti-doping requirements, and can accept long-term uncertainty in results and ranking and are willing to prepare for a path after retirement.

Conditions for pausing investment first: you have not yet completed a full season or a stage of competition under formal rules and referees, or you can only explain your ability through a single result; also do not treat an amateur hobby, short-video popularity or a short training camp as proof of professional competitive qualification. Do not handle medication and injury on your own.

Education and training must be checked separately: BLS lists the entry-level education for this occupation as no formal education requirement and the on-the-job training as long-term on-the-job training; O*NET lists 27-2021.00 as Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), and among respondents 35% consider less than high school necessary, 24% a bachelor's and 23% high school or equivalent. But registration, selection, competition eligibility, anti-doping and medical boundaries are determined by local law and event rules, and this page provides no standard for selection, competition, medication or return to play.

In one sentence: this is an occupation whose core is training continuously under established rules and taking part in formal competitions while being responsible for one's own competitive performance and compliance boundaries. Competence depends on training execution, body management, rule compliance and teamwork, not talent labels or a single result.

The work of athletes and sports competitors falls into four categories: training and physical condition (taking part in training as planned, maintaining fitness and nutrition, and recovering and preventing injury under the guidance of the team doctor and coach); competition execution (competing under the established rules and tactics, recording and analysing performance, and reviewing and adjusting afterwards); equipment and support (maintaining the equipment and protective gear of the sport, using venues and facilities according to procedure, and reporting safety hazards); and representation and collaboration (representing the team or club at media and public events, serving as captain, and working with coaches, team doctors, agents and sponsors). All four categories are premised on complying with competition rules, anti-doping regulations and medical boundaries.

O*NET27-2021.00 Athletes and Sports Competitors (updated 2026, Bright Outlook) has the duty of competing in athletic events. The actual 9 tasks include post-competition evaluation, equipment maintenance, training as planned, fitness and nutrition, competing according to the rules, being guided by coaches/athletic trainers, pre- and post-competition deployment, public events and captain duties. details has Importance ratings, with post-competition evaluation 80 and maintaining equipment and training as planned 79; these are not task frequency or an individual threshold and do not mean everyone carries out all of them.

Adjacent occupations may all involve the same sport, but their goals, responsibilities and rule boundaries differ.
Competitive performance in formal competition
In a formal competition meeting the entry and eligibility requirements, completing the competition according to the rules and tactics and leaving reviewable training and performance records.
Training plans, competition rules and equipment

The objects are the training and competition plan, one's own physical state, the equipment and protective gear of the sport, and competition venues and facilities; the basis is the competition rules, anti-doping regulations, event and institutional procedures, and the judgement of the team doctor and coach.

Athletes and sports competitors (US side O*NET 27-2021.00, Athletes and Sports Competitors) take part in organised, referee-officiated athletic events to compete before an audience. The official duty is Compete in athletic events; BLS describes it as competing in organised, referee-officiated athletic events to entertain an audience. Typical tasks include competing in events or athletic sports under established rules, training under the guidance of a coach or athletic trainer to improve skill and fitness, taking part in training as planned, maintaining optimal fitness through regular training and a nutrition plan, evaluating and adjusting performance after a competition, maintaining the equipment of the sport, accepting pre-competition deployment and discussing performance afterwards, and representing the team or club at media, speaking and public events and serving as captain when necessary. The occupation in the United States has no formal entry-level education requirement and long-term on-the-job training, and O*NET lists 27-2021.00 as Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0). Mainland China statistics aggregate by industry sector and do not list this occupation separately, so industry figures can only serve as a broad comparison and cannot be taken as income for this occupation. This page does not constitute advice on selection, competition, contracts, medical matters, nutrition or individual anti-doping cases.
Training—competition—review
Train as planned and record → manage fitness and recovery → compete according to the rules → analyse and review performance → adjust the subsequent training and competition arrangements.
Reviewable training and competition records
Training and appearance records, competition results and review notes, compliant medication and medical treatment records, and equipment and safety inspection records.
The athlete and the team

Training execution, competition conduct and anti-doping responsibility are borne by the athlete; injury treatment, medication and competition eligibility are decided by the team doctor, the event and the institution according to the rules.
Education and training

BLS lists the entry-level education as no formal education requirement and the on-the-job training as long-term on-the-job training; O*NET lists 27-2021.00 as Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), and among respondents 35% consider less than high school necessary, 24% a bachelor's and 23% high school or equivalent. The actual pathway usually starts from youth competition and squad training, and the specific standard is set by the sport, the league and local rules.

Training experience, registration eligibility, competition eligibility, a professional contract and anti-doping compliance are different states: an amateur result does not automatically bring professional registration, and signing a contract does not mean obtaining competition eligibility or an exemption from the rules.

At least six items must be verified before starting or signing: the occupational measure and sport entity (O*NET 27-2021.00 is the US measure, and in mainland China the sport, the team and the competition system must be identified); registration and competition eligibility requirements; anti-doping regulations and testing procedures; the medical boundaries for injury, medication and return to play; contract, agency and commercial rights terms; and the pay and season structure (basic pay, bonuses, sponsorship and self-employment).
Occupational measure

On the US side it is O*NET 27-2021.00 (Athletes and Sports Competitors); in mainland China the sport, the professional team or club and whether it is a professional event or a registration-based competitive system must first be identified, because the registration, pay and management rules differ greatly between sports.
Education and training pathway

BLS lists no formal education requirement and long-term on-the-job training; in practice the main line is youth training and squad competition, and some sports enter higher levels through school or university teams, with the pathway and age window set by the sport's rules.
Registration and competition eligibility

Registration, transfer and competition eligibility are decided by the sport association, league and event rules; before applying, check the registration requirements, age and eligibility limits and the transfer and representation rules, which cannot be inferred directly from an adjacent occupation or amateur experience.
Anti-doping and medical boundaries

The prohibited list, therapeutic use exemptions and testing procedures are set by the World Anti-Doping Agency and the local anti-doping organisation; injury diagnosis, medication and return-to-play decisions must be made by qualified medical personnel, and are not handled on one's own.
Contracts and commercial rights

The employment contract, agency representation and sponsorship endorsements involve different rights; before signing, check the term, pay structure, image use, termination and dispute resolution clauses and keep the written text.
Pay and working hours

Posts with the same title may use basic pay, appearance fees, bonuses, sponsorship or self-employment; when comparing, include the season length, income fluctuation, injury stoppage and retirement arrangements, taxes and agency fees in the written conditions, not only the nominal annual salary.

subject.summary: Athletes and sports competitors train continuously under established rules and take part in formal competitions as planned, and are responsible for physical condition, injury, equipment and compliance boundaries. On the US side this corresponds to O*NET 27-2021.00 (Athletes and Sports Competitors, Bright Outlook), with no formal entry-level education requirement and long-term on-the-job training; mainland China statistics aggregate by industry sector and do not list this occupation separately, and do not cover competition prizes, sponsorship or self-employed income.
